scope: Proposition 7.1 (Collision criterion) of the manuscript “A counterexample to Hadwiger's conjecture” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-Hadwigers-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 157 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a97293542586d351), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 37-38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let σ be a unit law in Theorem 3.1, and let e σ be a restriction of it of relative mass at least 2−o(N), decomposed into leaves satisfying (4.7). Mix the leaves with their actual masses in e σ. Suppose accepted numerical queries as above, with their leaf-pair choices of table and separate filters, satisfy Eindependent leaf pair Z dAdB dνn ≥ 2−o(N) . (7.3) Then two independent units from the original σ have all four cross holes with probability at least 2−(kmax+.03)N−o(N) . (7.4) 37 It suffices to obtain (7.3) after skipping some leaf pairs, or after summing over a bounded number of numerical options. Positive subsequential constants and inverse-polynomial overlap bounds both suffice. In particular, this conclusion contradicts a sequence violating Theorem 3.1.
